_comment: Documented divergences of the Go engine against the event_stream corpus. Fail-closed: a failing case NOT listed here is red; a listed case that starts reproducing the reference verdict is red (stale baseline); a listed case that never ran is red. Divergence class of the 4.3.2 corpus regen: the reference generation environment does not have the optional guard_agent module installed, and the reference engine builds every middleware-bus SecurityEvent through guard_core._pydantic_plugin_mute.get_telemetry_model('SecurityEvent'), which imports guard_agent; the construction raises ModuleNotFoundError inside the bus send path, the bus logs it and swallows it, so the reference capture seam records ZERO envelopes for every bus-emitted scenario (verified live against the reference engine: the events harness captures 0 events for these same cases today). The corpus therefore pins expected: [] for them. The Go event bus has no guard_agent import barrier and delivers its envelopes to the same capture seam, so it reports N events where the corpus pins 0. This is a corpus-generation environment artifact, not a Go detection or blocking bug: matching the reference byte-for-byte would require the Go engine to stop emitting events, which would degrade the engine. The four corpus cases that pin real envelopes (evt_detection_engine_callback_error, evt_pattern_anomaly_statistical, evt_pattern_anomaly_slow_execution, evt_pattern_anomaly_timeout) pass unchanged, and the single corpus-advisory case (evt_decoding_error_unreachable) is skipped by design. If the corpus regenerates in an environment with guard_agent installed, these scenarios pin real envelopes again and every entry below must be re-evaluated (stale entries are red by policy).
